elements.evidence: grants to Client, its affiliates and its contractors acting on Client's behalf

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: its contractors acting on Client's behalf
Grant remains a bare 'non-exclusive license to use the Interface'; no perpetuity language added
No 'irrevocable' wording appears anywhere in the redline

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: No termination limitation inserted in section 2(a) or elsewhere
or to a successor in interest in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assigning party's assets
grants to Client, its affiliates ... a non-exclusive license; coverage is unconditional, so the notice condition is unnecessary

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in interest in connection with a merger, acquisition

elements.element: No at-will revocation of the licence remains
elements.evidence: official check: no at-will revocation remains — ok

offending_extra_words: reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assigning party's assets
a successor in interest in connection with
reasons: Locked target was preferred, but the redline delivers only affiliate/contractor scope and successor transfer; the perpetual and irrevocable character of paid-up licences and the 'terminable only for uncured material breach' limit on subscription licences are entirely absent from the operative text.
Fallback is satisfied on its material terms: affiliates are covered (unconditionally, which is broader than 'on written notice') and assignment to an M&A successor is permitted without consent.

Minimality fails: operation 2 rewrites the whole carve-out and adds 'reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of the assigning party's assets', going beyond the M&A successor concept when a short phrase such as 'or to a successor in a merger or acquisition' would suffice; the official minimality gates also failed on expansion and changed-character ratio.

Intent is preserved: the non-obligation/competitive-freedom sentence, business-purpose scope and mutual consent requirement in section 15 remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
